subject: Private VPC deployment — networking clarifications & next steps
messages:

Subject: Private VPC deployment — follow-up & requested networking details

Hi Sarah — great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking through Acme's use case and the compliance constraints. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) Deployment mode: you confirmed a Private VPC (Redwood Private) is the preferred approach for production due to PCI scope and data residency. You also mentioned wanting an on-prem option evaluated for cold storage of logs — we can scope that separately.

2) Networking: we covered two connectivity options you asked about: AWS PrivateLink vs VPC peering. Preliminary notes: PrivateLink provides private, cross-account endpoints with no route table changes on your side; VPC peering gives direct routing but requires route table updates and shared CIDR planning. We should know your preference and whether cross-account endpoints are allowed by Acme's networking policy.

3) IP allowlists: you asked about static egress IP ranges for our control plane egress to your monitoring endpoints and callback URLs. We can provide a CIDR set for allowlisting, but for Dedicated/Private we typically provision elastic NAT IPs per deployment.

4) Security/compliance: you asked for SOC 2 and data retention details — I'll attach the network diagram you requested and share the SOC 2 summary in a separate thread (we'll also put full artifacts into the secure drive folder).

Attachments: acme-network-diagram.pdf (PDF)

Action items / next steps:
- Sarah: confirm preferred connectivity (PrivateLink vs VPC peering) and share any networking constraints (blocked ports, disallowed peering).
- Tom: confirm if Acme requires dedicated external IPs for callbacks and list the listener IPs we should expect to reach.
- Marissa/Dev: we'll provide a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and technical checklist after Dev reviews your network diagram.

Can we target a follow-up technical call next Tue (10/6) at 10am PT? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and invite our infra lead.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and for the diagram. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Connectivity: Prefer PrivateLink if possible. Our security team generally avoids VPC peering with external vendors due to CIDR overlap risks. PrivateLink would be ideal because it keeps traffic on the AWS backbone and avoids routing changes.
- IP allowlist: We need a stable set of IPs for egress callbacks (webhooks) and monitoring. Can you provide a list of static IPs or a small CIDR block? If PrivateLink is used, will we still need to allow external IPs, or will traffic stay within AWS and be covered by the endpoint?
- Ports: We allow outbound 443 and 22 to vendor endpoints; no other outbound ports are open by default.

I've attached a sanitized network diagram and the IP ranges for our VPCs (acme-network-diagram.pdf, acme-ip-allowlist.csv).

Yes to a technical call on Tue 10/6 10am PT — Tom and I will be there. Please invite your infra lead and anyone needed for the PrivateLink setup.

Best,
Sarah
Sr. Cloud Network Engineer
Acme Retail

Thanks Sarah — this is perfect and very helpful. A couple quick answers and I'll loop in our infra lead (Rishi) for the tech call: 

- PrivateLink: yes, with PrivateLink the traffic to our service stays on the AWS network. You will create an interface endpoint in your VPC and the traffic won't traverse the public internet. In that configuration, you typically do not need to add an external IP allowlist for the data path, but there are still management/control-plane callbacks (for billing/webhooks) that may originate from our control plane; we can minimize those with customer-hosted webhook endpoints inside your VPC if preferred.

- Static IPs: for callbacks outside the endpoint scope we can provide a small set of elastic NAT IPs. I'll confirm the exact CIDR/ips in the MAP before the technical call.

- Ports: 443 is sufficient for the PrivateLink data path. If we need SSH back to any management VMs for troubleshooting, we'll coordinate a temporary open window (and use jump hosts).

I'll send a calendar invite for Tue 10/6 10am PT and include Rishi. In the meantime, Dev, can you give a brief checklist for what we'll need from Acme (certificate, endpoint names, VPC ID, subnet IDs for interface endpoints, SG rules)?

—
Marissa

Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment — follow-up & requested networking details

Hi all — quick tech checklist for the PrivateLink path; I'll be on the call Tue to walk through these.

1) VPC & subnets: VPC ID, preferred AZs and subnet IDs (minimum 2 subnets in separate AZs for HA). Subnets must be private subnets with available ENI quota.
2) Security groups: we'll provide a recommended SG for the endpoint; you'll need to allow inbound HTTPS (443) from the endpoint ENIs or your app subnets.
3) Endpoint interface names: we don't require a certificate on your side for the interface endpoint, but if you want mTLS for additional security we can support it — we'll need your CA cert chain.
4) Route53: recommend a private hosted zone record to point the Red-API endpoint to the endpoint interface IPs (optional but simplifies DNS resolution).
5) IP allowlist: for any callbacks that do originate from our control plane (billing/webhooks), provide an endpoint inside your VPC or allowlist our elastic NAT IPs. We'll provide the exact IPs 48 hours before cutover.

Notes/limitations:
- VPC peering is still possible but will require CIDR non-overlap; given your preference for PrivateLink this is unlikely to be necessary.
- There may be a short maintenance window for initial provisioning (we'll coordinate).

I'll attach a short checklist PDF after the call.

Thanks — Dev
Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
